p: the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin: Meaning, the inhabitants of Samaria, whom the king of Assyria had placed in the place of the ten tribes, 2Ki 17:24,19:37. They professed God but worshipped idols and therefore were the greatest enemies to the true servants of God.
but we ourselves together will build: For they knew their pretence, that is to erect idolatry instead of true religion.
hired counsellors against them: They bribed the governors under the king to hinder their work, thus they that hinder cannot understand that God would be purely served.
Ahasuerus: He was also called Artaxerxes which is a Persian name, some think it was Cambises Cyrus' son, or Darius, as in Ezr 4:5.
Artaxerxes wrote Bishlam: Called Artaxerxes, which signifies in the Persian tongue an excellent warrior.
Dinaites: These were people whom the Assyrians placed in Samaria instead of the ten tribes.
Asnappar brought over: Some think it was not Sennacherib, but rather Salmanasar.
river: That is, Euphrates, and he means in respect to Babel that they dwelt beyond it.
at such a time: Or Cheeneth, who were a certain people who envied the Jews.
custom: Meaning, the gifts that are wont to be given to kings when they pass by any country.
Peace: Or Shalom, salvation or greeting.
at such a time: Or, Cheeth, also called Cheeneth as in Ezr 4:10.
ceased the work of the house: Not altogether for the prophets exhorted them to continue but they used less diligence because of the troubles.
